motions.motion: Councilmember Gray moved to approve the Consent Agenda removing items 11.A. and 14.B. to be placed on the Scheduled Items for further discussion and removing Item 14.D from the Agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Approve the consent agenda, minus three items
motions.summary: The council approved its batch of routine items, pulling two out for separate discussion — including the water and sewer rate changes — and dropping one from the agenda entirely.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents by itself. The one thing worth noticing is that the utility rate item was pulled out of the routine batch so it could be discussed on its own.

motions.item_title: Adopt Change Order #1 with Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services, LLC for the Wastewa…
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Change Order #1 with Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services, LLC for the Wastewater Treatment Plant Upgrade. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change order on the sewer plant upgrade
motions.summary: The council approved the first change order with the engineering firm Advanced Engineering and Environmental Services on the city's sewer plant upgrade; the motion does not state a cost.
motions.impact: Nothing changes day to day. This is a contract adjustment on work already underway at the sewer plant, and with no dollar figure given, it is not clear whether it adds to the project's cost.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule for Water Rates, Sewer Rates, and Utility Billing Rates and Fees.
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain City Consolidated Fee Schedule for Water Rates, Sewer Rates, and Utility Billing Rates and Fees. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Water and sewer rate changes taken up
motions.summary: The council took up changes to the city's water, sewer, and utility billing rates, but the record does not list the new rates or the outcome.
motions.impact: Every household on city water and sewer would feel a rate change. But this record does not say which rates moved or by how much, so nothing here tells you what your bill will be.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the Porter's Crossing Master Development Agreement 15.B. ORDINANCE/PUBLIC HEARING - An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to Porter's Crossing Master Development Plan and Rezoning of 1 lot from Open Space to R1
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Item 15.B., an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to Porter's Crossing Master Development Plan and Rezoning of 1 lot from Open Space to R1. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Rezone one Porter's Crossing lot from open space to homes
motions.summary: The council rezoned a single lot in Porter's Crossing from open space to R1 residential and updated the development plan to match.
motions.impact: One lot in one neighborhood: ground that was zoned open space in Porter's Crossing can now hold a home. If you live next to it, expect a house where the plan showed open space; the rest of the city is unaffected.

motions.item_title: A Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the Porter's Crossing Master Development Agreement
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt Item 15.A., a Resolution of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Fourth Amendment to the Porter's Crossing Master Development Agreement. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Change the Porter's Crossing development deal
motions.summary: The council approved the fourth change to the city's development agreement with Porter's Crossing, the contract that sets what can be built there.
motions.impact: If you live in or near Porter's Crossing, this is the contract half of a paired decision — the zoning change itself is the next item. On its own it changes nothing you would see.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Seventh Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget
motions.motion: Councilmember Burnham moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Approving the Seventh Amendment to the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year Annual Budget. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Final adjustment to last year's city budget
motions.summary: The council approved a seventh round of amendments to the 2024-25 budget, adopted two weeks before that budget year ended.
motions.impact: Routine housekeeping — nothing changes for residents. Amendments like this are the bookkeeping the city does to close out a year, and the motion does not say which line items moved.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Budget and the Certified Tax Rate
motions.motion: Councilmember Wood moved to adopt an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Adopting the Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Budget and the Certified Tax Rate. Councilmember Clark seconded the motion.
motions.headline: Adopt the 2025-26 city budget and tax rate
motions.summary: The council adopted Eagle Mountain's spending plan for the year that starts July 2025 and set the city's property tax rate at the certified rate.
motions.impact: This is the city's main money decision of the year, setting what gets funded through June 2026. The certified rate is the no-increase rate, so the city is not raising its overall property tax take, though your own bill still shifts with your home's value.
